correctness.rationale: For all n≥2 and t>0 over real scalars, a norming sign vector gives the quadratic defect inequality. Explicit Cauchy–Schwarz minimization by signed support masses and arithmetic–geometric mean yields the dimension-balanced coefficient c. A fully specified positive/negative group witness attains equality and yields unit pairs realizing the exact Day modulus for 0≤ε≤2/sqrt(1+c). At larger ε, equality would force |m|≥|d| coordinatewise, contradicting the squared norm identity; compactness makes the gap strict. This covers zero coordinates, even/odd n, 0 and 2 endpoints as indicated. The finite checker passed 12 rational identities and 67536 seeded numeric cases, but no universal inference is made from finite tests.

value.rationale: The exact best midpoint curvature coefficient and the maximal exact initial interval of the classical Day modulus are natural quantitative invariants of an infinite family of real Banach spaces, not textbook deductions from equivalent norm inequalities. The signed-support reduction both explains the parity-dependent optimizers and identifies complementary supports as the geometric boundary of equality. The result gives information beyond qualitative uniform convexity or a finite numerical gain; no unrelated downstream theorem is asserted.
